title: The forms of a reply

# The forms of a reply

flowdown reads GitHub's Markdown and, over it, the forms an agent's reply is made of: a callout,
steps, tabs, figures, the case for and against, a folded section, sources. Both of flowdown's
parsers read them: the npm package's and the Rust crate's. This file is what they agree on. Its
examples are written as CommonMark's are, but what follows the `.` is not HTML: it is the forms
the text holds, one a line, as both parsers' tests print them.

A form is a quote whose first line is a marker. It is asked for by that marker and never
guessed; one with nothing it can take stays the quote it was written as, and in any other
Markdown reader the whole of it is a quote and a list, still readable.

## Markers

The markers, their names written in capitals, are read whatever their case. Both parsers' tests
read this table and fail when their own list of markers differs from it.

| Marker | Form | What it takes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[!NOTE]` | callout | the quote |
| `[!TIP]` | callout | the quote |
| `[!IMPORTANT]` | callout | the quote |
| `[!WARNING]` | callout | the quote |
| `[!CAUTION]` | callout | the quote |
| `[!STEPS]` | steps | the list after it |
| `[!TABS]` | tabs | the headings after it, up to a rule or a shallower heading |
| `[!STATS]` | stats | the list after it |
| `[!PROS]` | pros | the list after it |
| `[!CONS]` | cons | the list after it |
| `[!DETAILS]` | details | the quote |
| `[!SOURCES]` | sources | the list after it |

## How a form is printed

A line names the form; a callout adds its kind. Then, quoted, its title: the rest of the
marker's line, or a tab's label. A form that takes a list ends with how many items it took. A
form inside another is printed under it, two spaces further in; a tab is inside its tabs. A text
that holds no form prints `(none)`.

## Callouts

GitHub's alerts. The words after the marker title it.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!WARNING]
> The migration locks the table.
.
callout warning
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!NOTE] Downtime
> The migration locks the table.
.
callout note "Downtime"
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!TIP]
> One.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Two.

> [!CAUTION]
> Three.
.
callout tip
callout important
callout caution
````````````````````````````````

A marker is read whatever its case.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!warning]
> Mind the gap.
.
callout warning
````````````````````````````````

A name that is no marker leaves the quote a quote, and so does a marker that is not on the
quote's first line.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!DANGER]
> Not a form.

> First line.
> [!NOTE]
.
(none)
````````````````````````````````

## Steps

Stages in order: the numbered list after the marker. It may follow the marker unquoted, as a
model writes it, or quoted with it.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!STEPS] Cut a release
1. **Run the checks.** Everything CI runs.
2. **Tag it.** `git tag v1.2.0`
.
steps "Cut a release" 2
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!STEPS]
> 1. **One**
> 2. **Two**
> 3. **Three**
.
steps 3
````````````````````````````````

A blank line may stand between the marker and its list.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!STEPS]

1. **One**
2. **Two**
.
steps 2
````````````````````````````````

A marker with nothing it can take stays the quote it was written as.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!STEPS] Plan

Just a paragraph.
.
(none)
````````````````````````````````

## Tabs

Variants side by side: each heading after the marker is a tab, its text the tab's label, up to a
rule or a heading shallower than the first.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!TABS] Install
#### macOS
`brew install jq`
#### Linux
`apt install jq`

---

After the tabs.
.
tabs "Install"
  tab "macOS"
  tab "Linux"
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!TABS]
### One
a
### Two
b
## Next section
c
.
tabs
  tab "One"
  tab "Two"
````````````````````````````````

A rule right before a heading of the first one's depth parts two tabs rather than ending them:
models write one between variants. It is not drawn.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!TABS]
#### npm
`npm i jq`

---

#### bun
`bun add jq`

---
#### pnpm
`pnpm add jq`

---

After the tabs.
.
tabs
  tab "npm"
  tab "bun"
  tab "pnpm"
````````````````````````````````

A tab holds forms of its own: a compared option, its sides.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!TABS]
#### PostgreSQL
> [!PROS]
- concurrent writes

> [!CONS]
- needs a server

#### SQLite
> [!PROS]
- no server
- one file

---
.
tabs
  tab "PostgreSQL"
    pros 1
    cons 1
  tab "SQLite"
    pros 2
````````````````````````````````

## Stats

Headline figures: the list after the marker, each item a figure and what it counts.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!STATS]
- **3.1x** faster
- **42 MB** less memory
.
stats 2
````````````````````````````````

## Pros and cons

The case for and the case against, each the list after its marker.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!PROS]
- typed APIs
- one binary

> [!CONS]
- a build step
.
pros 2
cons 1
````````````````````````````````

## Details

Secondary material, folded under its title: what the quote holds.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!DETAILS] Full log
> The long part, quoted.
.
details "Full log"
````````````````````````````````

## Sources

The pages a reply draws on: the list of links after the marker.

```````````````````````````````` example
> [!SOURCES]
- [Page title](https://example.com/page)
- [Another](https://example.org/)
.
sources 2
````````````````````````````````

## A reply

The forms as a reply holds them, one after another.

```````````````````````````````` example
The migration takes an hour.

> [!WARNING] Downtime
> The table is locked while it runs.

> [!STEPS] Run it
1. **Stop the writers**
2. **Migrate**

> [!STATS]
- **1 h** to migrate
- **0** data lost

> [!SOURCES]
- [Runbook](https://example.com/runbook)
.
callout warning "Downtime"
steps "Run it" 2
stats 2
sources 1
````````````````````````````````

<!-- END TESTS -->
